severity_rationale: C4 Low: DoS requiring a reverting external contract (dispatcher hook). C4 guidance: 'DoS requiring attacker control of an external contract → often Low.' Here the hook is a trusted sibling, but liveness-coupling means any hook bug (or temporary pause) DoSes stake/unstake/claim. Principal remains recoverable via emergencyWithdraw (confirmed by spec). Accrued rewards are forfeited only if the user chooses emergency exit during the DoS window, and the DoS is bounded by owner responsiveness (setDispatcherHook(0)). No direct theft; principal is never at risk. Classified Low per C4 external-contract-DoS guidance.
title: stake / unstake / claim revert when dispatcherHook.pull() reverts, forcing users through emergencyWithdraw and forfeiting rewards
description: _syncBudget is invoked at the top of stake(), unstake(), and claim(). When dispatcherHook is set to a non-zero address, _syncBudget makes an external call to dispatcherHook.pull() with no try/catch. If the dispatcher hook reverts (bug, upgrade breakage, griefing, or intentional pause in the sibling yield-claim-nft module), every user-facing non-emergency path reverts. Users keep principal but cannot claim rewards or unstake normally until the owner either fixes the hook or clears it via setDispatcherHook(address(0)).
attack_path: 1) Owner (or governance flow) sets dispatcherHook = H. 2) H's pull() begins reverting (e.g., H is paused, H's own dependency is broken, H is maliciously upgraded, or caller-gated check fails because NFTStaker is not wired as recipient). 3) All stake/unstake/claim calls revert at _syncBudget -> dispatcherHook.pull(). 4) Users must either wait for owner intervention or exit via emergencyWithdraw, forfeiting accrued rewards (compounds with DEDUP-007 / ECON-002 to produce permanently stranded tokens). 5) Owner action required (setDispatcherHook(0) or hook repair) to restore normal flow. Combines with DEDUP-007 (setDispatcherHook does not drain old hook) for a compound failure: a broken hook forces emergency exits, and swapping hooks strands any accrued mint-debt.
impact: Temporary denial-of-service of stake/unstake/claim and forced forfeiture of accrued rewards for any user who cannot wait and uses emergencyWithdraw. Principal is never at risk (emergencyWithdraw skips _syncBudget per spec, confirmed at line 305-317), but accrued rewards are socially/economically lost. Severity bounded by owner responsiveness.
recommendation: Wrap dispatcherHook.pull() in try/catch so a reverting hook degrades to a no-op instead of DoSing the whole call. Example: `try dispatcherHook.pull() returns (uint256 delta) { /* use delta */ } catch { /* skip, continue with current budget */ }`. Preserves the escape-hatch property while making stake/unstake/claim hook-independent.

sanitization.rationale: Verified: root cause is in NFTStaker.sol _syncBudget (line 208: `dispatcherHook.pull();` with no try/catch). The hook itself being able to revert is normal external-call behavior; defensive wrapping is NFTStaker's responsibility. Not a 'parent/forked contract OOS' case. The hook is a trusted sibling but liveness-coupling without a try/catch is the in-scope bug.
